Definition: apparently a primary verb (properly, θρέχω; compare G2359); which uses δρέμω (the base of G1408) as alternate in certain tenses; to run or walk hastily (literally or figuratively):--have course, run.
BiblicalUsage: Paul runs his race for the prize, and he prays that the word of the Lord may have free course and be glorified. Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receives the prize? So run, that ye may obtain — and Paul asks prayer that the word of the Lord may have free course and be glorified.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two runnings are one life: the runner runs for the prize, and the word runs to be glorified, and both are to be run without stopping.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
